concerns.text: T011/T012/T013 explicitly state 'NO fallback to synthetic or product-structure data' and 'EXCLUDE rows... with NO fallback mechanism'. This directly contradicts FR-008 and the Plan's 'Provenance Proxy filtering; fallback to Structure-Verified' strategy. The task list silently weakens the spec's requirement to handle missing kinetic data by introducing a hard exclusion that the spec does not mandate, violating the 'no silent constitution drift' principle.

T031 specifies a 'single model-level permutation test (N=200)'. The Plan explicitly requires 'Permutation test within CV loop' to ensure robustness against fold-specific overfitting. A single model-level test is a semantic weakening of the planned methodology, failing to satisfy the statistical rigor required by FR-004 and the Plan's complexity tracking.

T016 only 'flags' classes with <50 samples. SC-005 requires measuring class balance against a specific metric (max/min <= 2) and ensuring no class is under-represented by more than a factor of 2. The task lacks the logic to calculate this ratio and enforce the constraint, dropping the acceptance criterion for SC-005.

FR-001 requires converting IR and NMR data into a 'single 512-bin fixed-length fingerprint'. T011 and T012 describe fetching and filtering IR and NMR data separately but lack a dedicated task to merge these sources into the unified fingerprint entity. This risks a pipeline that produces disjoint datasets, failing to satisfy the core data entity definition in the spec.

FR-007 requires Benjamini-Hochberg correction on 'per-bin' p-values. T031 performs a model-level test, and T031a extracts 'feature importance scores' (not p-values). T032 then attempts BH correction on these scores. The task chain fails to generate the required per-bin p-values, breaking the statistical significance pipeline defined in FR-007 and the Plan.
